title: Add contextual retry metadata and unified error-envelope for streamed tool invocations
author: Evelyn Park
description:
Motivation: Streaming tool/function calls and the OpenAI-compat shim have grown ad-hoc error behavior that makes retrying and diagnosing failures brittle across clients. We continue to see operational incidents where transient capacity pressure or proxy timeouts present inconsistent hints (Retry-After header vs 429 without metadata), and tool-calls that stream partial frames lack deterministic idempotency signals. This PR introduces a unified, backward-compatible error envelope and a small set of deterministic retry/context fields to improve client-side retry logic and server-side observability.

What changed (high level):
- Introduced a stable error envelope for both HTTP and streaming SSE frames: {code, message, details[], retry_context? , idempotency?}. The envelope is surfaced inline for JSON responses and as a structured frame type inside the stream protocol (frame.type = "error").
- Added retry_context fields: retry_after_seconds (float), retry_token (opaque string), and retry_scope ("request"|"model"|"region"). Retry tokens are optional hints clients can surface when reattempting to preserve fairness in throttling. Servers may emit a Retry-After header for legacy clients in parallel.
- Exposed idempotency diagnostics: idempotency_key (if supplied), dedupe_window_ms, and conflict_policy ("reject"|"merge"|"last-write"). This allows streaming tool-calls to indicate whether a resumed attempt is safe or requires manual resolution.
- OpenAI-compat shim mapping: 429/RateLimit scenarios now map to error.code = "rate_limit.exceeded" with retry_context populated where available. Earlier ambiguous 503/504 cases are categorized into transient vs gateway errors to provide clearer client semantics.
- Runtime and adapter changes: streaming adaptor emits structured error frames and stamps retry_token and idempotency info into internal traces and emitted metrics. We added an opt-in backward-compatibility mode that emits legacy headers only, for customers still relying on header-only semantics.
- SDK surface updates (Python/TS): introduced a small helper to parse the new envelope and a RetryPolicy class that prefers retry_token if present and falls back to Retry-After header.
- Tests and docs: end-to-end integration tests for resumed streamed tool-calls, unit tests for mapping logic, and comprehensive API docs describing the envelope and example client handling.

Why this approach:
- Deterministic retry behavior reduces duplicate tool side-effects when clients resume streaming calls after network interruptions.
- A unified envelope supports both sync HTTP calls and streaming frames without fragmenting client logic across transports.
- Retry tokens allow the platform to make smarter decisions about fairness and throttling while giving clients an opaque hint to coordinate retries.

Compatibility notes:
- Backward compatible: clients that ignore the envelope will continue to see the previous status codes and legacy headers (when in compatibility mode). New clients should prefer the envelope and retry_token.
- For non-idempotent tool calls (no idempotency key supplied), the server will still attempt best-effort safety but will set conflict_policy="reject" and include explicit guidance in message.

Commits (summary):
- 8a3f9d9: Add streaming error frame types and parsing helpers in runtime adapter
- b1d27ee: Implement unified error envelope and retry_context schema in API layer
- c9f4a12: Map OpenAI-compat shim responses to new envelope and update shim tests
- d4e6b3f: Add SDK helpers (python + ts) and docs for retry handling
- f5a2210: Integration tests for resumed stream tool-calls and idempotency diagnostics
- 4e8c91b: Add e2e canary that validates rate-limit tokens under load

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/adapter/streaming_error_envelope.go - core envelope framing and streaming frame emitter
- api/handlers/error_envelope.go - HTTP mapping layer and compatibility mode toggle
- adapters/openai_shim/mapping.md - spec for how legacy OpenAI codes map into the envelope
- sdk/python/redwood/errors.py - parsing helpers + RetryPolicy
- sdk/typescript/src/retry.ts - TS helper for retry_token and Retry-After fallback
- docs/api/error_handling.md - user-facing doc and examples for resumed streams and idempotency
- tests/integration/stream_tool_retry_test.py - e2e test simulating interrupted stream and resumed invocation

CI notes:
- First run failed: flaky integration test under test harness (ordering of frames). Fixed by making the frame ordering assertion tolerant to interleaved heartbeat frames (commit f5a2210).
- Lint and unit suites passing on second run. Canary perf test showed negligible CPU impact (~1.8% median p99 increase) from emitting extra envelope frames; metric-backed rollouts planned.

Review thread (high level):
- Marcelo: requested clearer guidance on when servers must emit retry_token vs when Retry-After header is sufficient. Action: added retry_scope and documented operator-controlled token emission.
- Diana: asked to ensure identity of retry_token is opaque and rate-limited; added tests to ensure tokens are not echoed back in logs and rotated on restart.
- Ralph: requested SDK ergonomics; added RetryPolicy and examples for both resumed streams and single-shot requests.
- Author response: implemented changes, clarified docs, and added compatibility-mode toggle for enterprise customers.

Rollout plan:
- Feature guarded behind a platform flag. Start with hosted beta customers for 2 weeks, run canary on redwood-dedicated pool with small percentage of traffic, monitor duplicate-tool-call counts, retry_token issuance rates, and p99 latency.
- After validation, flip default to enabled and publish SDK patch releases with migration notes.

Release notes (user-facing):
- New: Structured error envelope for HTTP and streaming responses. Prefer the envelope for robust retry handling.
- New: retry_context (retry_after_seconds, retry_token, retry_scope) and idempotency diagnostics for streamed tool calls.
- Note: Backward compatible; legacy headers still emitted in compatibility mode.

Operational impact:
- Improved diagnostic signals for incidents caused by transient capacity pressure.
- Small increase in emitted frame bytes and trace metadata; accounted for in performance canary.

Follow-ups (future work):
- Server-driven adaptive retry windows (produce stronger server-side guidance when in sustained pressure).
- Rollout an operator tool to reconcile idempotency_key collisions across retries.
- Post-rollout: remove compatibility header-only mode after 6 months with deprecation notice.

If you want to test locally: see docs/api/error_handling.md for example stream client code and sdk/python/redwood/examples/resume_stream.py
